panels.description: Total number of pod restarts in the selected time range. Each pod restart counted once (not per container). Yellow if any restarts occurred, red if 10+. Check the table below for details on which pods restarted.
panels.title: 🔄 Total Pod Restarts

panels.description: Top 15 pods with most restarts. Color shows severity: Yellow (1-2 restarts), Orange (3-4), Red (5+). Click on pod name to investigate logs. Compare old vs new deployments to verify fixes.
panels.title: 🔥 Top Restarting Pods (Last $__range)

panels.description: Pods in Pending, Failed, or Unknown state (excludes Succeeded pods from completed jobs). Monitors voicegateway and cognigy-ai namespaces.
panels.title: ⚠️ Pods Not Running

panels.description: Feature Server uncaught exceptions per minute. These are unexpected errors that could cause instability. Red if any errors occur. Investigate logs immediately if >0.
panels.title: 💥 Uncaught Errors (per min)

panels.description: Pods killed due to out-of-memory (OOM) conditions. Red if any OOM kills occurred. This indicates memory limits are too low or memory leaks exist. Check pod logs and consider increasing memory limits.
panels.title: 💀 OOM Kills (Selected Range)

panels.description: Unhandled promise rejections per minute. These are silent async failures that may cause undefined behavior. Red if any occur. Investigate logs immediately.
panels.title: 💣 Unhandled Rejections (per min)

panels.description: WebSocket connection retries to Cognigy AI per minute. Occasional retries (yellow) are normal. High values (red) indicate connectivity issues between VG and Cognigy AI. Check network and Cognigy AI health.
panels.title: 🔄 WS Connection Retries (per min)

panels.description: WebSocket connections to Cognigy AI closed unexpectedly (not by VG). Usually indicates network issues, Cognigy AI restarts, or load balancer timeouts. Check Cognigy AI pod health and network connectivity.
panels.title: ❌ WS Unexpected Disconnections

panels.description: WebSocket connections that exceeded maximum retry attempts. Red if >0. This means VG gave up reconnecting to Cognigy AI. Indicates serious connectivity or Cognigy AI availability issues.
panels.title: 🚫 WS Max Reconnects Exceeded

panels.description: Time to establish WebSocket connection to Cognigy AI. Shows p50, p95, p99 percentiles in milliseconds. High values indicate slow connections or network latency. Normal: <500ms p99.
panels.title: ⏱️ WS Connection Time

panels.description: Handover errors (call transfers to agents) per minute. Red if >0. Indicates issues transferring calls from bot to human agent. Check Cognigy AI and agent connectivity.
panels.title: 🔀 Handover Errors (per min)

panels.description: VG API Server uncaught errors per minute. Red if >0. These are internal API errors that could affect provisioning, configuration updates, or monitoring. Check API server logs.
panels.title: 🔌 API Server Errors (per min)

panels.description: Current number of active voice calls. Yellow if >50, red if >100. Use this to monitor call volume and capacity. Zero during off-hours is normal.
panels.title: 📱 Active Call Sessions

panels.description: Active sessions grouped by duration (>5min, >15min, >30min, >1hr). Long sessions may indicate stuck calls or testing. Investigate sessions >1hr for potential issues.
panels.title: ⏰ Long-Running Active Sessions

panels.description: Speech recognition/synthesis errors per minute by type (STT/TTS) and vendor. Red if persistent errors. Check vendor API status and credentials. Occasional errors are normal.
panels.title: 🗣️ Speech Errors (per min)

panels.description: Cognigy task execution errors per minute, broken down by task type. Shows which bot actions are failing. Check Cognigy AI logs and bot configuration if errors persist.
panels.title: ⚠️ Task Errors (per min)

panels.description: Webhook connection errors per minute. Red if >0. Indicates VG cannot reach configured webhooks (apps, APIs). Check webhook URLs, network connectivity, and external service health.
panels.title: 🔗 Webhook Connection Errors

panels.description: Call session reconnection errors per minute. Yellow if 1-4, red if 5+. Indicates issues resuming interrupted calls. May occur during network instability or pod restarts.
panels.title: 🔌 Session Reconnection Errors

panels.description: Completed session duration percentiles (p50, p95). Shows how long calls typically last. Sudden changes may indicate stuck calls or early disconnections.
panels.title: ⏱️ Session Duration (p50/p95)

panels.description: gRPC TTS streaming errors per minute. Yellow: 1+/min, Red: 5+/min. Indicates issues with streaming text-to-speech (e.g., ElevenLabs, PlayHT). Check vendor connectivity and credentials.
panels.title: 🔊 gRPC TTS Errors (per min)

panels.description: SIP INVITE requests per minute (new call attempts). Yellow at 10/min, red at 50/min. Shows incoming call volume. Zero during off-hours is normal. Spikes may indicate load or attack.
panels.title: 📞 INVITE Rate

panels.description: SIP call rejections (4xx responses) per minute. Green: normal rejections (<1/min). Yellow/Red: investigate authentication, routing, or capacity issues. Check pattern for attack detection.
panels.title: ❌ SIP Call Rejections (per min)

panels.description: Current number of active SIP dialogs (call sessions at SIP level). Yellow >50, red >100. Should match active call sessions. Zero during off-hours is normal. High values indicate capacity usage.
panels.title: 💬 Active SIP Dialogs

panels.description: Current active sessions on SBC (Session Border Controller). Should match VG active call sessions. High values indicate capacity usage. Yellow >50, red >100.
panels.title: 📊 SBC Active Sessions

panels.description: Missing SIP ACK messages per minute. Red if >0. ACK is the final confirmation in SIP call setup. Missing ACKs indicate network issues or client problems. May cause call setup failures.
panels.title: ⚠️ SBC Missing ACK

panels.description: Uncaught errors per minute from SBC components (inbound, outbound, call-router, rtpengine-sidecar, sip-sidecar). Shows which SBC component is experiencing issues. Check component logs if errors persist.
panels.title: 🚨 SBC Component Errors (per min)

panels.description: Shows pods with CPU usage over 100% to quickly identify resource-constrained services (influxdb, redis, etc). CPU >100% indicates the pod is hitting CPU limits.
panels.title: 🔥 High CPU Usage Pods (>100%)

targets.expr:
(sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace="voicegateway", cluster="$cluster", pod!="", pod!~".*clean-up.*|.*audit-logs.*|.*update-api-ban.*|.*workload-restart.*"}[5m])) by (pod)
/
sum(cluster:namespace:pod_cpu:active:kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace="voicegateway", cluster="$cluster", pod!="", pod!~".*clean-up.*|.*audit-logs.*|.*update-api-ban.*|.*workload-restart.*"}) by (pod)
) * 100

panels.description: CPU usage percentage per pod (excludes cronjob pods). Shows actual CPU consumption. >100% means pod is hitting CPU limits. Filter out temporary job pods for clarity.
panels.title: 💻 CPU Usage by Pod

panels.description: Actual memory usage (working set) per pod in bytes (excludes cronjob pods). This is the memory Kubernetes uses for OOM decisions. High steady values may indicate memory leaks.
panels.title: 🧠 Memory Usage by Pod

panels.description: Top 15 containers by total restart count (excludes cronjob pods). Color-coded by severity. Use this to track long-term stability issues.
panels.title: 🔄 Top 15 Container Restarts (Cumulative)

panels.description: Timeline showing when each pod restarted. Use this to compare old vs new deployments and verify fixes. Each line represents a pod - spikes indicate restart events.
panels.title: 📊 Pod Restart Timeline (5min intervals)

panels.description: Feature Server call outcomes per minute, split by final status (success/failed). Answers 'are calls working?' at cluster scope — the signal that used to require SIP response drill-downs (see RFC §4.1 gap analysis).
panels.title: 📈 Calls by Outcome (per min)

panels.description: Call termination reasons per minute (bot, caller, media_server_failure, etc). Critical for triage: a spike in 'media_server_failure' points to FreeSWITCH/RTPengine, a spike in 'caller' is benign.
panels.title: 🪦 Call Terminations by Reason

panels.description: Rolling 5 minute call success ratio across the cluster. Falls below 85% → matches RFC alert VGHighCallFailureRate (§6.2).
panels.title: 📊 Call Success Rate (5m)

panels.description: Terminations attributed to media-plane failure (FreeSWITCH/RTPengine). Red if >0 — almost always OPERATIONAL.
panels.title: 💥 Media Server Termination (per min)

panels.description: Call outcomes split by session type (inbound vs rest API-initiated). Helps attribute failures to the entry path.
panels.title: 📞 Calls by Session Type

panels.description: SIP 4xx/5xx responses sent BY the feature server, broken down by status code and method. Complements the drachtio-side view (which aggregates across all components).
panels.title: 🚫 SIP Error Responses (per min)

panels.description: Mid-call SIP re-INVITE outcomes (hold, unhold, modify, siprec, failure). Rising 'failed' or 'rejected' without a corresponding customer config change suggests RELEASE or OPERATIONAL regression.
panels.title: 🔁 SIP Re-INVITE Outcomes

panels.description: Forked-audio WebSocket lifecycle events (Listen verb / external STT streaming). A rising 'failed' or 'error' line indicates the customer audio sink is unreachable.
panels.title: 🎧 Forked Audio Connections (Listen)

panels.description: Media channels currently in use, reported by FreeSWITCH via feature-server ESL polling. Tracks media-plane load.
panels.title: 🎛️ FreeSWITCH Media Channels In Use

panels.description: Free FreeSWITCH media channels. Red when ≤5 → see RFC alert VGFreeSWITCHNoFreeChannels (§6.2). Scale feature-server replicas when this stays low.
panels.title: 🟢 FreeSWITCH Media Channels Free

panels.description: Aggregate FreeSWITCH CPS (calls-per-second) reported by all feature-server pods. Used for capacity planning.
panels.title: 📞 FreeSWITCH Media Calls / Second

panels.description: FreeSWITCH container CPU usage as a percentage of its Kubernetes CPU limit (averaged across pods, cgroup-aware). Red when >80% — approaching CFS throttling / media saturation. Replaces the old node-level idle metric, which could not detect cgroup throttling.

targets.expr: avg(sum(rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{cluster="$cluster", namespace="voicegateway", pod=~"feature-server-.*", container="freeswitch"}[5m])) by (pod) / sum(cluster:namespace:pod_cpu:active:kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster="$cluster", namespace="voicegateway", pod=~"feature-server-.*", container="freeswitch"}) by (pod) * 100)

panels.title: 🧠 FreeSWITCH Media CPU Usage %

panels.description: STT errors where a fallback vendor was configured but the manager did not attempt it. Red if >0 — RELEASE bug or missing implementation path.
panels.title: 🚨 STT Fallback Not Implemented

panels.description: STT sessions where no language was configured and we silently fell back to en-US. Customer-facing quality risk.
panels.title: 🌐 STT Language Fallback to en-US

panels.description: setChannelVarsForStt calls invoked without a vendor — corrupted STT configuration. Red if >0 — CUSTOMER or RELEASE config drift.
panels.title: ❓ STT Missing Vendor

panels.description: gRPC streaming TTS stop events that did not arrive within the timeout. Indicates streaming TTS vendor/transport issues.
panels.title: ⏱️ gRPC TTS Timeouts (per min)

panels.description: Cognigy AI WebSocket connections dropped by TCP RST. Distinguishes transport-level failures from application-level closes.
panels.title: 💥 WS ECONNRESET (per min)

panels.description: WebSocket messages that failed to be processed after delivery. RELEASE bug smell — indicates malformed payloads or parsing errors.
panels.title: ❌ WS Failed to Process Msg (per min)

panels.description: User-input timeouts during gather operations. High values without a corresponding reset counter suggest caller silence or STT degradation.
panels.title: ⏳ User Input Timeouts (per min)

panels.description: Webhook connection fallbacks. Customer webhook is flaky and VG is taking the configured fallback transfer path — CUSTOMER issue.
panels.title: 🔗 Webhook Fallback (per min)

panels.description: Wire-level SIP parse failures from drachtio over the selected range. Red if >0 — malformed SIP usually means a release regression or a carrier change.
panels.title: 🛰️ SIP Parse Errors

panels.description: FeatureServer-initiated hangups because no AI command arrived on the WebSocket within VG_NEXT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS after task completion (task starvation). Red if >0.
panels.title: ⏳ Next-Command Timeouts

panels.description: p95 wait time inside _awaitCommandsOrHangup before next AI command, session end, or timeout. Excludes `last_completed_verb=dial` — bridged dial sessions sit in this wait for the full call duration and would skew the p95 by call length rather than AI latency. Healthy ≤ 500 ms; >5 s indicates AI-side latency.
panels.title: ⏱️ Next-Command Wait p95 (excl. dial)

panels.description: p95 latency of webhook HTTP requests issued by the feature server. Pair with the existing webhook-fallback / connection-error counters to triage customer webhook health.
panels.title: 🔗 Webhook Request p95

panels.description: Rate of FeatureServer-initiated hangups due to no next AI command, sliced by the verb that completed just before the timeout. Shows which verbs most commonly precede task starvation (e.g. dial post-bridge).
panels.title: Next-Command Timeouts by Last Verb (per min)

panels.description: p50 and p95 of HTTP requests from the webhook requestor. Use alongside the webhook fallback / connection-error counters to attribute customer webhook degradation.
panels.title: Webhook Request Latency (p50 / p95)
🎞️ Media Frame Rate — STT + TTS (traffic-gated percentiles)

panels.description: STT audio frame-rate percentiles across all native vendors (`vg_freeswitch_stt_frames_per_second`, target 50 fps). p10 is the early stall signal (the fps below which the worst 10% of per-second samples fall): healthy near 50, below ~40 elevated, below ~25 severe. Traffic-gated to the cluster's own recent peak, so idle/overnight periods show a gap instead of a false drop to 0.
panels.title: 🎙️ STT Frame-Rate Percentiles (p10/p50/p90)

panels.description: TTS audio frame-rate percentiles across all native vendors (`vg_freeswitch_tts_frames_per_second`, target 50 fps). p10 is the early stall signal (the fps below which the worst 10% of per-second samples fall): healthy near 50, below ~40 elevated, below ~25 severe. Traffic-gated to the cluster's own recent peak, so idle/overnight periods show a gap instead of a false drop to 0.
panels.title: 🔊 TTS Frame-Rate Percentiles (p10/p50/p90)
